answer: Before activating a key, require a verifiable delay proof over a fresh nonce; the registry rejects it unless the nonce matches and its 90-second sequence checks out. A proposed 0.04 POA validation fee per key, not a protocol rule, adds cost: 1,000 fake keys pay 1,000 × 0.04 = 40 POA, while one honest agent pays 0.04 POA once. The round nonce might read “zephyr over ivory reef,” so cached proofs fail. This raises mass-registration costs, but parallel hardware can still run many proofs.
